title: Can it preserve progress through a close pass?
utterance: Find a close oncoming pass where the robot preserves at least 90% of baseline speed using less than 15 degrees heading excursion. Return before, closest-pass and after evidence, including whether the people changed course. Compare with another oncoming encounter in the same recording with at least 30% speed loss; report if no qualifying comparator is confirmed.
requiredClauses: Speed >=90% baseline and heading excursion <15 degrees
Comparator is same-recording oncoming encounter with >=30% speed loss
returnRequirements: Episode span, clause evidence, and event anchor times.
hardNegativeRecipe: Nearest lidar range from food truck; compare following episode with oncoming encounter without flagging mismatch.
capabilityGaps: Close physical separation and human trajectory may remain uncertain; no claim of safety from speed preservation.
evidencePolicy: Judge raw time-aligned messages; captions and discovery spans are candidate leads, not relevance truth. Mark unresolved clauses UNKNOWN.

candidateContrasts.reason: Close oncoming pass with steady plotted mean speed; check all numeric and trajectory clauses.
Large slowdown is reported while following someone; this may fail the oncoming comparator requirement. Do not silently substitute it.

behaviorValue: Test whether retrieval distinguishes steady close passing from a larger slowdown in the held-out crowd recording.

judgingPlan.unit: one intent evaluated against one distinct episode
judgingPlan.selection: Single-episode query: strongest candidate and one clause-specific near miss, with one reserve. Comparison query: two intended comparison members and one reserve or hard negative.
judgingPlan.stopRule: Stop at the cap even if all candidates fail or remain unknown. Report no confirmed positive in the judged pool; do not infer no match in the recording or widen judging automatically.
judgingPlan.reuse: Merge overlapping windows; reuse decoded evidence across intents while judging each intent separately.

title: Does it respond differently to a crowd and a staircase?
utterance: Compare one crowd pass and one stair climb in Bass_Garage with corridor range below 0.3 m. Show which physical surfaces generate the close returns and how robot speed differs. State what the missing main front camera prevents you from resolving.
requiredClauses: Associate returns with people/structure or mark unknown
Compare speed over equal 4 s spans
returnRequirements: Episode span, clause evidence, and event anchor times.
hardNegativeRecipe: Treat equal range as equal risk; substitute body-camera count for absent main-front detections.
capabilityGaps: Raw range is not calibrated clearance or safety; body cameras may not disambiguate all reflectors.
evidencePolicy: Judge raw time-aligned messages; captions and discovery spans are candidate leads, not relevance truth. Mark unresolved clauses UNKNOWN.

candidateContrasts.reason: Crowd pass: verify close-range threshold and which object produces the return.
Stair slowdown: compare supported range and speed with the crowd episode; two intended comparison members, not a positive/negative pair.
People above the stairs can make reflector identity ambiguous; reject an overconfident stairs-only attribution.

behaviorValue: Test whether similar close-range signals can be interpreted in their physical context, with missing-camera limits preserved.
